name: Uber (cited by Portal26.ai)
problem_summary: Uber rolled out Claude Code access to ~5,000 engineers in December 2025. Usage nearly doubled by February 2026, 84% of developers were classified as agentic coding users by March, and by April the company had burned through its entire 2026 AI budget — four months in. The CTO acknowledged being 'back to the drawing board' on AI spend governance.
amount_mentioned: Entire annual AI budget (specific figure undisclosed)

name: Unnamed Enterprise (cited by Portal26.ai)
problem_summary: A separate enterprise reportedly spent $500 million in a single month after deploying AI access with no usage caps. Microsoft simultaneously began canceling most internal Claude Code licenses, citing runaway token bills that made consumption unsustainable at scale.

name: Unnamed Healthcare Enterprise (cited by Portal26.ai)
problem_summary: A healthcare enterprise consumed one trillion tokens over six months, generating more than $6 million in unplanned costs. The finance team didn't understand what was driving the spend until well after the fact — costs were invisible by design, accumulated through normal agent activity that no one had instrumented or governed.

name: CloudAtler (Muthupandian A)
problem_summary: Autonomous AI agents can get stuck in infinite loops retrying failing tasks — a single agent using OpenAI o1 at $60/1M tokens can consume $20–50 per hour. Scale to a fleet of 500 concurrent agents in a CI/CD pipeline and you can burn $25,000 in a single night. Runaway agent spend is cited as the #1 cause of budget variance in AI engineering teams for 2025.

name: nthypes (HN user, Founder & CTO of AI-First CRM)
problem_summary: Spent $928.45 on AI coding agents (Cursor/Claude) over 70 days. Reports that 340M tokens felt wasteful — models using 50K tokens exploring dead ends for solutions that could have been expressed in 5K tokens. Calls out that at $5,500+/year per developer, AI coding changes the unit economics for early-stage startups and the pricing model hasn't stabilized.

name: satgate (HN user, 25+ years enterprise security)
problem_summary: Describes the agent cost problem as fundamentally economic, not technical. Most teams discover their agent burned through $10K in API calls only after the invoice hits — there's no identity, authorization, or cost control layer for machine-to-machine traffic. Calls agentic AI 'the Wild West' until governance catches up.

name: CharlesW / YouTube (Morse Code Hack)
problem_summary: A security researcher demonstrated how hidden Morse code in prompts tricked an AI agent into spending $200K autonomously. The critical variable identified is not intelligence level but permission scope combined with reversibility of agent actions — agents with broad financial access can be exploited.

name: Gábor Horváth / Hiflylabs
problem_summary: Describes Denial of Wallet (DoW) and OverThink attacks on LLM APIs where a single malicious prompt can cost 3,000x more than a normal request. Reasoning-token attacks can force models to generate up to 46x more hidden thinking tokens than needed. Clients came to Hiflylabs after internal pilot API bills did things 'nobody signed off on' — and that was just enthusiastic internal users, not malicious actors.
amount_mentioned: 3,000x cost variance per request, up to 46x reasoning tokens

name: Larridin / Forrester (Greg Zorella)
problem_summary: Forrester analyst Greg Zorella warned that one AI agent can 'go crazy' and consume the budget of nine other agents. Larridin enterprise scans find an average of 47 orphaned agents per organization — agents still running after the project ended, the pilot completed, or the team moved on, with no owner accountable for spend.
amount_mentioned: 1 agent consuming 9 agents' worth of budget; 47 orphaned agents average per org

name: Prefactor.tech (AI cost governance startup)
problem_summary: Documented a case where an agent's cost per task tripled in one week with no code change — traced to a knowledge-base update that made one retrieval step return far more documents, causing context to grow on every subsequent turn. Most teams only see aggregate monthly totals, not per-agent or per-step cost attribution, making it impossible to connect spend to outcomes.
amount_mentioned: Cost per task tripled (specific dollar amount undisclosed)
